title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A sharp portrait of wealth, longing, and illusion in the Jazz Age.
longDescription: The Great Gatsby explores class, desire, love, and the collapse of the American Dream through the mysterious figure of Jay Gatsby and his obsessive devotion to Daisy Buchanan.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: A deeply human story of justice, racism, and moral courage.
longDescription: Set in the American South, this novel follows Scout Finch as her father, Atticus Finch, defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime.

author: George Orwell
description: A chilling vision of authoritarianism, surveillance, and truth manipulation.
longDescription: 1984 presents a totalitarian society ruled by fear, propaganda, and control, where language, memory, and freedom are constantly distorted by the state.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: A witty and enduring story of class, character, and love.
longDescription: Pride and Prejudice follows Elizabeth Bennet as she navigates social expectations, family pressure, and her evolving relationship with Mr. Darcy.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: A beloved adventure through courage, wonder, and Middle-earth.
longDescription: Bilbo Baggins leaves the safety of home on an unlikely quest involving dwarves, dragons, treasure, and personal transformation.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: An epic sea voyage shaped by obsession, vengeance, and symbolism.
longDescription: Captain Ahab’s relentless hunt for the white whale becomes a profound meditation on fate, madness, nature, and the limits of human will.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: A psychological study of guilt, morality, and redemption.
longDescription: The novel follows Raskolnikov, a young man who commits murder and spirals through inner torment, moral conflict, and existential crisis.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: A monumental novel about history, family, war, and society.
longDescription: War and Peace interweaves the lives of aristocratic families during the Napoleonic Wars, exploring human nature and historical change.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: A story of resilience, independence, and emotional depth.
longDescription: Jane Eyre traces the development of an orphaned girl into a self-aware woman who values dignity, love, and moral integrity.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: A foundational work of Gothic fiction and early science fiction.
longDescription: Victor Frankenstein’s attempt to conquer death results in tragedy, raising enduring questions about ambition and responsibility.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: A comic and profound masterpiece about illusion and idealism.
longDescription: Don Quixote follows a man who reinvents himself as a knight-errant, producing one of literature’s great reflections on imagination and dignity.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
description: A tragedy of grief, revenge, hesitation, and existential inquiry.
longDescription: Prince Hamlet navigates betrayal, mortality, and revenge in one of literature’s most influential tragedies.
